title: Jana Nayagan Advance Booking Surges as Thalapathy Vijay's Political Swansong Nears July 23 Release
excerpt: Pre-sales for Vijay's final film have crossed 26,000 tickets in under 24 hours, with trade analysts projecting a 100-crore worldwide opening day for the Tamil political action thriller.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Jana Nayagan, Thalapathy Vijay's final film, releases on July 23 after delays and controversies.
  • Advance bookings surpassed 26,200 tickets and ₹1.54 crore gross within 24 hours.
  • Analysts predict a ₹100 crore worldwide opening day, marking Vijay's third century opener.
  • Vijay's political success has heightened anticipation for his cinematic farewell.

  • Jana Nayagan (Hindi: Jan Neta), Thalapathy Vijay's final film, releases on July 23 after months of delay caused by censor board issues and a controversial 'A' certificate
  • Pre-sales have crossed 26,200 tickets and ₹1.54 crore gross in under 24 hours, with most bookings coming from Karnataka and Kerala while Tamil Nadu shows remain limited
  • Trade analysts project a potential ₹100 crore worldwide opening day, which would mark Vijay's third century opener after Leo and The Greatest Of All Time
  • Vijay's political ascent — his Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam party won the 2026 Tamil Nadu elections — has amplified buzz for what fans are treating as a grand farewell

After months of delays, legal battles, and an online leak that threatened to derail the entire project, Thalapathy Vijay's swansong Jana Nayagan is finally headed to theatres on July 23. And if advance booking numbers are any indication, the Tamil superstar's farewell to cinema will be as thunderous as his entrance into politics.

Pre-sales for the Tamil political action thriller crossed 26,200 tickets and approximately ₹1.54 crore gross at the Indian box office within the first 24 hours of bookings opening, according to trade tracking data. The figures are particularly striking given that Tamil Nadu — Vijay's home state and by far his largest market — had only 13 shows listed at the time, with full-scale bookings expected to open in the days ahead.

A Film That Survived Everything

Jana Nayagan's journey to the screen has been anything but smooth. Originally scheduled for a January release, the film was delayed indefinitely after failing to secure censor board clearance. When it finally received certification, the 'A' (adults only) rating raised eyebrows — unusual for a mainstream Tamil commercial film aimed at Vijay's broad fan base.

Then came the leak. The entire film surfaced online weeks before its theatrical date, a blow that would have sunk most releases. But Vijay is not most actors, and Jana Nayagan is not most films.

Directed by H. Vinoth and produced by Venkat K. Narayana under KVN Productions, the film stars Vijay alongside Pooja Hegde, Bobby Deol, and Mamitha Baiju. It is rumoured to be a partial remake of Nandamuri Balakrishna's Telugu hit Bhagavanth Kesari, recast as a Tamil political drama that mirrors Vijay's own real-life journey from screen to statehouse.

Projected Opening Day Success
›Projected ₹100 crore worldwide opening day
›Third century opener for Vijay after Leo and The Greatest Of All Time
›Political momentum from Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam's 2026 election win
›Karnataka leads with 58% occupancy in pre-sales

The Political Mileage Factor

What has truly turbocharged Jana Nayagan's prospects is Vijay's real-world political breakthrough. His party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), swept the 2026 Tamil Nadu assembly elections in a result that stunned political observers. The actor-turned-politician is now poised to lead the state as Chief Minister — a storyline that makes his final film feel less like entertainment and more like a coronation.

Trade analysts project that the political momentum could push Jana Nayagan past ₹100 crore worldwide on opening day, which would make it Vijay's third century opener following Leo and The Greatest Of All Time. Karnataka has been the early leader in pre-sales, contributing ₹1.35 crore gross with 58% occupancy, while Kerala has added ₹16 lakh.

The Hindi Wild Card

The film will also release in Hindi under the title Jan Neta. Vijay has a growing audience in Hindi-speaking markets — Leo earned ₹2.85 crore net on its Hindi opening day — but limited promotional efforts for the dubbed version may cap its potential. The title change itself could dilute awareness, a pattern seen with other dubbed releases.

Still, analysts estimate Jan Neta could open between ₹1.75 and ₹2 crore net in Hindi, which would place it among the top 10 Hindi openings for a Kollywood film.

What's Next

All eyes are now on Tamil Nadu's booking numbers, which will determine whether Jana Nayagan joins the ₹100 crore club on day one. For Vijay's global fan base — and for the diaspora audiences who have followed his career from Pokkiri to politics — July 23 is shaping up as a farewell worth celebrating.
